title: The pigeonhole principle over a finite set, with an explicit colliding pair
statement: Let s and t be finite sets over the naturals and g a function on the naturals. If the size of t is strictly less than the size of s, and g sends every member of s to a member of t, then there exist two DISTINCT members a and b of s with g a = g b.

formal.statement: theorem Nat.Finset.exists_collision : ((x0 : AxNat.Finset) -> ((x1 : AxNat.Finset) -> ((x2 : ((x2 : AxNat) -> AxNat)) -> ((x3 : AxNat.lt (AxNat.Finset.card x1) (AxNat.Finset.card x0)) -> ((x4 : ((x4 : AxNat) -> ((x5 : Eq.{1} Bool (AxNat.Finset.memB x0 x4) Bool.true) -> Eq.{1} Bool (AxNat.Finset.memB x1 (x2 x4)) Bool.true))) -> Exists.{1} AxNat (fun (x5 : AxNat) => Exists.{1} AxNat (fun (x6 : AxNat) => And (Eq.{1} Bool (AxNat.Finset.memB x0 x5) Bool.true) (And (Eq.{1} Bool (AxNat.Finset.memB x0 x6) Bool.true) (And (Not (Eq.{1} AxNat x5 x6)) (Eq.{1} AxNat (x2 x5) (x2 x6)))))))))))

evidence.notes: The trusted gate cannot tell a THEOREM's statement is not what its name says: a `card_le_of_injOn` with its two `card`s transposed, an `exists_collision` whose pair need not be DISTINCT, or a `pigeonhole` whose strict inequality points the other way would each be admitted, carry an empty axiom footprint, and pass every other row in this ledger. `nat_prelude/finset_pigeonhole_tests.rs` instantiates each statement at a concrete pair of sets whose cardinalities are computed independently, and pairs every positive with the wrong statement it rules out. Three of its controls are the sharper kind, where a hypothesis cannot be DISCHARGED (`infer` must fail) rather than a conclusion merely being false.

notes: The STRONG form. This kernel has no funext, no propext and no classical choice, so the pair cannot be extracted from F:nat-finset-pigeonhole's refutation -- nothing turns a negation into an existential by logic. What does turn it is a DECISION PROCEDURE, and injectivity on the members of a Nat.Finset has one because the domain is bounded and equality on the naturals is decidable. The proof decides a bounded double search over [0, bound s) and uses both directions of the loop: at true, F:nat-finset-all-below-true-at reflects it back to the Prop injectivity that F:nat-finset-pigeonhole refutes, so that case is impossible; at false, F:nat-finset-all-below-false-witness yields the two indices and the three Bool guards are peeled to give the four components. Nat.beq's two reflection lemmas close it in opposite directions -- eq_of_beq_eq_true on the images, ne_of_beq_eq_false on the indices. The loop is written INLINE and is not a named Definition: nothing in the statement mentions it. ADR-1593.
